approach: With air resistance, the effective deceleration going up is larger than g, and the effective acceleration coming down is smaller than g, so the times are unequal.

steps.text: Going up, both gravity and air resistance act downward, opposing the upward motion.
Coming down, gravity acts downward but air resistance acts upward, opposing the downward motion.
A larger deceleration going up brings the ball to rest sooner, while a smaller net acceleration coming down means it takes longer to return to the ground.

common_mistakes.text: Ignoring air resistance and assuming the upward and downward motions are symmetric, giving T₁ = T₂.
